practice.title: Follow the Plan
practice.description: Always implement according to the validated plan, tasks, and checklist. Do not deviate without documenting the reason and escalating if necessary.

practice.title: Incremental Implementation
practice.description: Build incrementally, validating each component before moving to the next. This allows for early detection of issues and easier debugging.

practice.title: Test as You Build
practice.description: Create and run tests alongside implementation. Don't wait until the end to validate functionality. Unit tests, integration tests, and validation scripts should be part of the implementation process.

practice.title: Document Deviations
practice.description: If implementation reveals that the plan or architecture needs adjustment, document the deviation clearly and escalate to the appropriate mode (Architect or Strategist) for resolution.

practice.title: Follow Project Standards
practice.description: Adhere to the coding standards, style guides, and conventions established in the project. Consistency is critical for maintainability.

practice.title: Write Clean, Readable Code
practice.description: Code should be self-documenting where possible. Use clear variable names, appropriate comments, and logical structure. Future maintainers (including yourself) will thank you.

practice.title: Handle Errors Gracefully
practice.description: Implement proper error handling, logging, and recovery mechanisms. Don't let errors cascade or leave the system in an inconsistent state.

practice.title: Optimize Appropriately
practice.description: Focus on correctness first, then optimize if needed. Premature optimization is the root of many problems. Profile before optimizing.

practice.title: Manage Dependencies Carefully
practice.description: Document all dependencies clearly. Use version pinning where appropriate. Ensure dependencies are compatible and don't introduce conflicts.

practice.title: Test Integrations Thoroughly
practice.description: Integration points are common sources of bugs. Test all interfaces, APIs, and module boundaries carefully. Verify data flow and error handling.

practice.title: Environment Consistency
practice.description: Ensure development, testing, and production environments are as similar as possible. Use containerization or environment management tools to maintain consistency.

practice.title: Comprehensive Test Coverage
practice.description: Aim for high test coverage, but focus on meaningful tests. Test edge cases, error conditions, and integration points. Don't just test the happy path.

practice.title: Automated Validation
practice.description: Automate validation wherever possible. Use CI/CD pipelines, automated tests, and validation scripts to catch issues early.

practice.title: Performance Testing
practice.description: Test performance under realistic conditions. Identify bottlenecks and resource constraints before they become production issues.

practice.title: Update Documentation
practice.description: Keep documentation in sync with implementation. Update README files, API docs, and inline comments as you build. Stale documentation is worse than no documentation.

practice.title: Document Decisions
practice.description: Record significant implementation decisions and their rationale. This helps future maintainers understand why things were done a certain way.

practice.title: Create Usage Examples
practice.description: Provide clear examples of how to use new features or APIs. Examples are often more valuable than lengthy explanations.

practice.title: Clear Progress Updates
practice.description: Provide regular updates on implementation progress. Report completed checklist items, blockers, and any issues discovered.

practice.title: Escalate Promptly
practice.description: Don't struggle in silence. If you encounter architectural issues, specification gaps, or strategic concerns, escalate to the appropriate mode immediately.

practice.title: Code Reviews
practice.description: When working in a team, participate in code reviews. Both giving and receiving feedback improves code quality and knowledge sharing.

practice.title: Security by Design
practice.description: Consider security implications during implementation. Validate inputs, sanitize outputs, use secure APIs, and follow security best practices.

practice.title: Secrets Management
practice.description: Never hardcode secrets, credentials, or sensitive data. Use environment variables, secret management systems, or secure configuration files.

practice.title: Dependency Security
practice.description: Regularly check dependencies for known vulnerabilities. Keep dependencies updated and use security scanning tools.

practice.title: Meaningful Commits
practice.description: Make atomic, logical commits with clear messages. Each commit should represent a single logical change that can be understood and reviewed.

practice.title: Branch Strategy
practice.description: Follow the project's branching strategy. Use feature branches for new work, and keep branches focused and short-lived.

practice.title: Clean History
practice.description: Keep commit history clean and meaningful. Squash or rebase when appropriate, but preserve important historical context.
